# shapes_probes.txt - R2D-SHAPES S6 (D-W8-1083) and S6-fix1: the probes of the example shapes, read on both systems
# (the Linux capture in the protocol and the two Windows captures); the drivers' tables fix how many. Format:
# tests/tools/image_probe.py ("<x> <y> <RRGGBBAA> [<tol>]", origin top-left, alpha included). Fixed BEFORE the data
# existed (GODS_LAWS.md L-43): every value comes from the geometry of the scene and the sRGB formula, never from a
# capture. No probe lies within 2 pixels of a curved or a slanted edge, so none depends on how a curve is cut into
# segments; the edges between the triangles of the hexagon D are not edges of the shape (two triangles that share an
# edge leave no pixel of it uncovered, OpenGL 3.3 core, 3.6.1). The scene is in the header comment of
# examples/shapes/shapes.cpp.
#
# WHAT THE PROBES PROVE: every piece is drawn, with its colour, where the scene puts it (to the limit below); where
# two probes straddle an edge along the axes, one pixel inside and the next outside, that edge to the pixel; the three
# caps, the three alignments, the two units, the two curve distances and the layer of the path; each of the six
# triangles of D; the radii of D, H and K to 3 pixels each way and the radius of L to 5; the way H turns. WHAT THEY DO
# NOT PROVE: a change that moves a curved or slanted edge less than about 2.5 pixels (2 pixels of margin from the true
# edge, plus half a pixel past the changed one), and, past that, what no probe was put to read: the corners of B and
# of C, the thickness of H and of the lines of I, and an up or down move of the centre of D, H, K or L.
#
# the background: the four corners and a point between the pieces; 0.2 encoded by the CPU = 124 = 0x7C
0 0 7C7C7CFF 1
639 0 7C7C7CFF 1
0 479 7C7C7CFF 1
639 479 7C7C7CFF 1
165 165 7C7C7CFF 1
#
# A, fill_rect: inside, the first column inside the left edge, the column before it, the last pixel inside, the column
#  after it
80 80 FF0000FF 0
20 80 FF0000FF 0
19 80 7C7C7CFF 1
139 139 FF0000FF 0
140 80 7C7C7CFF 1
#
# B, fill_quad (the diamond): the centre, a point near the left corner, a point of its bounding box outside it
240 80 00FF00FF 0
190 80 00FF00FF 0
185 25 7C7C7CFF 1
#
# C, fill_triangles: near each corner, the colour of that corner dominates. The space the colours are blended in is
#  not a public promise, so each value is the middle of the two answers (blend the sRGB-encoded colours, or blend the
#  linear light and encode) and the tolerance covers both, plus 2
345 136 F41C1DFF 23
400 27 1AF31FFF 24
455 136 181CF5FF 23
#
# D, fill_indexed_triangles (the hexagon): the shared centre, a point near the corner at +x, a point outside; the
#  centre of each of the six triangles the 18 indices name, in the order of the list, each more than 2 pixels from its
#  three edges, so a triangle lost from the list fails its own probe; a point 2 pixels inside the left corner and one
#  2 pixels outside it (the radius, 60, held to 3 pixels each way)
560 80 FFFF00FF 0
612 80 FFFF00FF 0
612 30 7C7C7CFF 1
590 97 FFFF00FF 0
560 114 FFFF00FF 0
530 97 FFFF00FF 0

# E, stroke_rect centered, white at alpha 0.5 over the background, blended in the encoded values (renderer_2d.hpp):
#  0.5 * 255 + 0.5 * 123.55 = 189.28, the byte 189 = 0xBD; the band on both sides of the left edge (x 30), the
#  top-left corner (covered ONCE, so the same value), the column before the band, the first column of the hole, the
#  middle of the hole
27 240 BDBDBDFF 2

# H, stroke_ellipse (radii 55 and 30, turned 30 degrees, 10 thick): the band where it crosses the horizontal and the
#  vertical line through the centre, the centre (the hole), a point above and one right of the band, each valid
#  whichever way the turn goes; then the way it turns: a positive angle turns from +x toward +y, clockwise on the
#  screen, so the far end of the long axis is down to the right (covered) and not up to the right (background); then
#  the radii, each held to 3 pixels each way: the long one near the end of the long axis, the short one near the band
#  above and below the centre

# L, the same circle from the renderer opened with a curve distance of 12 pixels: ceil(pi / acos(1 - 12 / 55)) = 5
#  sides, a corner at +x (as draw2d_shapes_parity_test, C14), so its left side is the vertical line 44.5 pixels left
#  of the centre: the point 49.5 pixels left is OUTSIDE the pentagon. The centre and a point near the corner at +x are
#  covered. On the same line, 2.5 pixels inside the left side and 3.5 pixels outside it: the radius held to 5 pixels
#  each way (3 pixels move a side of the pentagon only 2.43 pixels, less than a probe can read under the margins)
